title: Christmas Photobooth — turn a clip into a studio-flash photobooth
uses: ✦ Made with Claude Pro · Opus 5.5 model
subtitle: Film yourself striking a few poses to a song, then let Claude Code add a red focus light, a flash on the beat and a black-and-white print that pops up over your face in every shot, just like a real photo booth. One prompt.
greeting: Thanks for commenting BOOTH 😊 Here's the full studio-flash photobooth prompt. Once your Christmas clip is ready, tag me so I can see it 🎄

sections.label: before we start
sections.heading: What you need
items: A clip with music
A vertical clip of you in several poses, each pose its own short shot, with the song already in the clip
Claude Code
Use the Claude app (Code tab) or Claude Code in the Terminal
One prompt
Copy it from below. No code, no manual editing
Same angle and distance every pose

Sit at the same distance with the camera at the same angle, so your face is the same size and in the same spot in every pose. The print frame then tracks your face smoothly and every photo looks equally good

sections.label: step by step
sections.heading: Follow these steps
items: Film your poses

Set the camera up vertically, face it and hold each pose for 1–2 seconds. Change pose and start a new shot, then add your song to the clip. A curtain or plain wall with warm light gives it more of a photo booth feel
Open Claude Code in the clip's folder
Make a new folder, put your clip in it (plus stills of the poses you want flashed, if any), then open that folder in Claude Code, either in the Terminal or the Claude app's Code tab
Paste the prompt and send
Paste the prompt below, tell Claude the clip's file name (or attach the clip) and press Enter. Claude finds each pose's cut, the song's beats and your face, then picks the sharpest frame in each pose
Check the preview first

Claude doesn't render the whole clip yet. It sends a strip of every shot with the print in place and a close-up of one print, along with the flash frame numbers. Reply OK if you like it, or ask for changes, like "less grain" or "pick another frame for pose 3"

items.alt: Claude Code showing a preview strip of every shot with flash frame numbers and a close-up print, waiting for OK
items.cap: Claude shows you every shot first. Reply OK and it renders the final file

items: Get your photobooth clip
You get an MP4 the same length as your clip with the song untouched. Every pose gets a red light, a flash and a warm black-and-white print with a torn black border, landing right over your face

items.alt: A warm black-and-white print with a black border placed over the face in the clip, brown curtain behind
items.cap: Film grain, a torn edge, and placed exactly over your real face

items: See every pose
Every pose where a face is found gets its own print, even when your hands cover part of your face. Post it as a Christmas reel, or grab a frame for your profile picture

items.alt: A row of black-and-white prints, one per pose, each placed over the face in the clip
items.cap: Every pose gets its own print, lined up like a photo booth strip

sections.label: copy-paste
sections.heading: Studio-flash photobooth prompt
sections.intro: Paste it into Claude Code. The last part (THINGS I CAN CHANGE) is what you can adjust; see how below
items: Studio flash photobooth

Turn my attached video into a "studio flash photobooth" edit, at normal
speed, synced to the song in the video.

INPUTS
- One source video with music (required).
- Optional: still images of the exact moments I want the flash on.

STEPS

1. Split the video into poses.
   - Detect hard cuts. Each stretch between cuts is one pose.
   - One flash per pose. Include every pose, even ones where hands cover
     part of the face, as long as a face is detected.

2. Find the beats.
   - Detect the song's beats (librosa beat tracking). Every flash must
     land exactly on a beat.
   - In each pose, pick the beat that scores best on: beat strength,
     face sharpness, low motion, face detected.
   - Spacing: the next flash must come at least 1 s (freeze) + 0.4 s
     (shortest red light) after the previous one. A freeze must end
     before the video ends.
   - If I attached stills, use those frames instead and snap each to
     the nearest beat.
   - Tell me the flash frame numbers.

3. Speed: normal. No slow motion. Keep the original audio untouched.
   The output must be exactly as long as the source.

4. Face and light point: detect the face in each flash frame (eyes,
   nose, mouth corners). Aim the light at the lower cheek on the side
   turned toward the camera: 35% of the way from the mouth corner up to
   the eye, pushed outward by 0.32 × the distance between the eyes.
   Track that point backward with optical flow so the light follows
   the face. Never track across a cut.

5. Lighting sequence before every flash:
   a. Red focus-assist light: soft gaussian spot, sigma 0.30 × eye
      distance, plus a faint halo 2.5× wider at 20% strength. Lift red
      toward saturation by up to 62%, cut green 16% and blue 20%. Scale
      by surface brightness so skin catches it and dark hair barely
      does. Fade in 3 frames, hold up to 15 frames with a very slight
      flicker, fade out 2 frames.
   b. Gap: 4 frames with no effect.
   c. Red light starts 24 frames before the flash. If the previous
      freeze or a cut is closer than that, start it later (minimum 12
      frames). Never move the flash.
   d. One frame where only the top 36% of the picture is flash-lit.
   e. Exactly ONE full flash frame: lift blacks to about 40/255, push
      midtones up hard (116 → 188, 208 → 243), cut saturation to about
      half, slightly cool, brightest on the subject. Then straight back
      to normal.

6. Freeze with print, straight after each flash:
   a. The next 30 frames (1 s) show the flash frame without the flash
      effect, frozen. These frames REPLACE the footage underneath so
      the audio stays in sync. Playback resumes at flash frame + 31.
   b. Over it, show the photo that was "taken": the flash frame
      (without the flash effect), styled and placed as below.

   PRINT COLOUR (black-and-white photobooth print)
   - Convert the cropped photo to grayscale, values 0–1.
   - Contrast: (value − 0.02) × 1.45, clip to 0–1.
   - Gamma: value ^ 0.82 (bright flash-lit skin, deep blacks).
   - Matte range: value × 0.86 + 0.07 (no pure black or pure white).
   - Vignette: darken the corners by up to 22%, smooth falloff from the
     centre.
   - Slight blur: 0.9 px.
   - Film grain: gaussian noise, strength 0.04, softened with a 0.7 px
     blur. The grain stays still for the whole freeze.
   - Warm tone: multiply blue by 0.84 and green by 0.93, leave red.
   - Border colour: near black (about 9/255), with the same warm tone
     and a very light grain.
   - Border size on an 800 × 1060 print: left 26 px, right 8 px, top
     34 px, bottom 68 px. The inner top edge is slightly rough (about
     ±5 px). From 72% of the width to the right edge it gets rougher
     (about ±9 px) and dips 6 px lower, like a torn corner. Soften the
     inner edge by 1.2 px.

   PRINT POSITION
   - Crop: centre on the face box. Crop width 4.6 × the distance
     between the eyes (capped at the video width), same aspect as the
     photo area (766 × 958). The face sits at 42% from the top of the
     crop. Keep the crop inside the frame.
   - Print size: 800 × 1060 px on a 1080 × 1920 video (74% of the
     width).
   - Rotation: 0.7° clockwise.
   - Placement: put the print so the face in the print sits exactly
     over the real face in the video, as if the print replaced the
     face. Keep it fully on screen: at least 24 px from the left and
     right edges and at least 60 px from the top and bottom.
   - Pop-in: fade in over 2 frames while scaling from 105% to 100%
     over 3 frames. Hard cut back to the footage after 1 s.

7. Output: one MP4, 1080 px wide for vertical video, 30 fps, H.264,
   original audio copied. Same length as the source.

BEFORE THE FULL RENDER
Show me a strip of every freeze frame with the print in place, and a
close-up of one print. Wait for my OK.

WHEN YOU DELIVER
Tell me the flash frames, which shots got a shorter red light, and
anything that differs from what I asked.

THINGS I CAN CHANGE
- Shots: [one per pose / my picks]
- Flash on: [every beat-aligned pose / every 2nd beat / my frames]
- Red light: [on / off], size [0.30 × eye distance]
- Freeze length: [1] second
- Print size: [74%] of width
- Print position: [over the face / exact centre, same spot every shot]

sections.label: make it yours
sections.heading: What you can change
sections.intro: Edit the brackets at the end of the prompt, or just tell Claude while you check the preview
items: Pick your poses
Shots: my picks, then attach stills of the poses you like. Claude flashes there and snaps each to the nearest beat
How often it flashes
Flash on: every 2nd beat if you want the flashes further apart
Red focus light
Red light: off for a clean flash only, or make the spot bigger, e.g. 0.40 × eye distance
How long it freezes
Freeze length: 1.5 or 2 seconds so people see the print longer
Print size
Print size: 60% for a smaller print that shows more of you, or 85% to fill the screen
Print position
Print position: exact centre puts the print in the same spot every shot, for a tidy album look

sections.label: tip
sections.heading: Tips
items: Face the camera so your eyes, nose and mouth are clearly visible for at least a moment in each pose. Claude has to find your face to place the print
Change poses with clean hard cuts rather than slow moves. Claude uses the cuts to tell the poses apart
Hold each pose for at least 1.5 seconds so there's room for the red light, the flash and the 1-second freeze
A song with a clear beat makes the flashes land better than a slow one. Try an upbeat Christmas song
Wear something festive: a scarf, a fluffy jacket or a Santa hat looks great as a vintage black-and-white print
Claude installs the tools it needs (like ffmpeg and librosa) by itself. If it asks for permission, just allow it
